video.title: Why Your Cold Emails Get No Replies (And How To Fix It)

summary: Will Cannon describes how he uses cold email to grow software businesses, including Uple, a B2B data product. He explains targeting, follow-up sequences, testing, deliverability, and how to combine cold email with other acquisition channels. The conversation also covers examples such as AI automation agencies, a tracking product for auto body shops, and a financial planner’s campaign to teachers. His main advice is to target a narrow audience with a timely, relevant offer, test the message and sequence, and avoid relying on one acquisition channel.

speakers.description: Founder of software businesses and cold email operator.

ideas.customer: B2B companies with sales teams that need prospect data, including SaaS companies and IT services firms.
ideas.problem: Sales teams need accurate, current contact data and ways to identify prospects who may be ready to buy.
ideas.offer: B2B data similar to ZoomInfo, with real-time email verification, intent signals, and free leads matched to a prospect's ideal customer profile.

pricing.model: Subscription; trial or free leads are used to introduce the product.

acquisition_channels.details: Will says cold email was the main early acquisition channel. Campaigns used a short message, competitor comparison, real-time verification as a differentiator, and an offer of a trial or 50 free leads.

acquisition_channels.details: Will says he started SEO, and later describes building a mini brand that appears for searches such as ZoomInfo alternatives.
Will says he started ads, but gives no specific campaign details.
Will says partnerships are among the channels the business uses now; no specific partnership is described.
Will says affiliates are among the channels the business uses now; no specific affiliate arrangement is described.
Will describes building a mini brand and name recognition so prospects find and remember Uple.

ideas.delivery: Customers build prospect lists in Uple, use intent signals to identify campaigns, and receive email data that is verified in real time. The customer then uses the data in its own outbound systems.
unit_economics_claims: Will says Uple reached its first 1 million AR almost entirely through cold email; the transcript does not state a period or spell out AR.
The subscription price, acquisition cost, gross margin, and customer count are not stated.

acquisition.how: Agents could identify and segment company prospects and draft campaigns, but UK cold email rules, targeting quality, deliverability, and domain reputation need review.

onboarding.how: Signup, product access, and data delivery can be handled by software, with occasional checks for account or data issues.

delivery.how: Lead search, email verification, and intent signals are software-delivered; people may need to review data quality and unusual cases.

billing.how: Subscription billing can run through standard software, with occasional human handling of disputes or failed payments.

support.how: Agents can answer routine product and data questions, with human escalation for account-specific or complex problems.

uk_applicability.notes: The B2B data product can serve UK companies, but prospecting data and outbound campaigns need to account for UK data-protection rules and PECR. Unsolicited marketing email to individuals and sole traders generally requires consent; cold email to corporate subscribers is allowed subject to applicable rules.

risks: Cold email deliverability is vulnerable to domain reputation changes and evolving mailbox-provider requirements.
A campaign aimed at the wrong recipient or with a weak offer may produce little response.
UK prospecting must distinguish corporate subscribers from individuals and sole traders and handle personal data lawfully.
Will sells Uple, so his claims about its performance and differentiators are promotional.

tactics.name: Define a narrow ideal customer profile
steps: Specify a narrow company type and size rather than saying the service is for anyone.
Add relevant qualifiers such as employee count, outbound sales team, and software used.
Identify the role of the owner or manager who can make the decision.

quote.text: I sell to SAS companies that have 50 to 500 employees that have outbound sales teams that use XYZ software.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Start with a small, relevant prospect list
steps: Build a list of 100–200 people to begin with rather than trying to send tens of thousands of emails.
Filter prospects by the defined customer profile and relevant buying signals.
Prioritize the right person, message, and timing.

quote.text: You can build a list of 100, 200 people to start with and if you send emails at the right time with the right message.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Use a multi-email sequence and test its length
steps: Create a sequence rather than sending only one email.
Try short early gaps, such as three to five days after the first email and two to three days after that.
Space later emails farther apart; the guest says the sequence may eventually move to weekly.
Test a single email against a multi-touch campaign with comparable prospect groups.
Use the sequence length that performs better for the particular segment.

quote.text: Test this yourself. Send one camp you have a thousand of these divide 500 500 send one campaign and just send one cold email.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Keep follow-ups short
steps: Use short follow-up messages rather than paragraphs.
Test simple prompts and avoid stale phrases that make the email look templated.
Adjust wording to the industry and audience.

quote.text: I like short. I like short. Yeah, I like Hey, you know, I like any interest question mark.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Write a concise first email with a clear offer
steps: Use plain text and keep the email to about three lines.
Say how the sender found the prospect and why they are reaching out.
Explain what the product does, how it differs, and the value to the recipient.
End with a low-friction call to action, such as a trial or free leads.

quote.text: One is like, here's how I found you, why I'm reaching out. Here's what I do, why it's different, how I can help you.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Use a free sample to reduce the first commitment
steps: Offer a product trial or a set of free leads that match the prospect's ideal customer profile.
Give the prospect a chance to see the product before asking them to subscribe.
Use the sample to create a clear next step if the prospect wants more.

quote.text: I'll give you free leads that match your ICP. Like do you want some free leads? And then we give them a little taste.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Use intent and company-change signals
steps: Build separate campaigns around competitor use, surging intent, a new vice president, or recent funding.
Send the selected prospects into outbound systems and use multiple touches.
Match the message to the reason the prospect is being contacted.

quote.text: We'll build out one around competitors. We'll build around surging intent. or build out a runaround they just hired a new VP or got funding.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Protect deliverability when sending email
steps: Warm up sending domains and monitor domain reputation.
Use separate sending domains and keep per-domain volume low when scaling.
Start at small volume, then increase only when infrastructure and deliverability are working.
Keep current on changes in mailbox-provider requirements.

quote.text: You got to watch your domain reputation you got to warm up your domains deliverability is a lot harder and things are changing all the time.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Diversify customer acquisition
steps: Continue a channel that works, but reserve time to build other acquisition channels.
Add channels such as SEO, ads, partnerships, affiliates, and outbound one by one.
Build a recognizable brand so prospects may search for or remember the company directly.

quote.text: Don't let one channel be your sole source of revenue for your business if you like I would put some percentage of my time.
quote.speaker: Will Cannon

tactics.name: Use contextual personalization for a specific segment
steps: Choose a segment that receives relatively few cold emails.
Reference a real relationship or context relevant to that group.
Invite the prospect to a call with a message that matches their situation.

quote.text: He cold emails teachers because his company has a relationship with some of these school districts.

tactics.name: Offer a free trial when the buyer is already looking
steps: Identify prospects who are already in the market for the service.
Describe specific deliverables and who the service has helped.
Offer a time-limited free trial, then discuss price if the work produces results.

quote.text: If it works and if if you get a better um more views and more clicks and more everything from the vid from the videos that we do, then we'll talk about the price.

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest speaks from operating experience and gives concrete campaign processes, sequence timing, tools, and examples. Many performance figures are self-reported or second-hand, some numbers are garbled or inconsistent in the transcript, and the host's market-size claims are unsourced.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Will sells Uple, offers cold email help, and directs listeners to free playbooks that collect email addresses. The host also includes promotional segments for TK Owners and an online domain service; those ad reads were excluded as business ideas.
